title: Home Purchase Financing Late Charge — Late History Multiplier
content:
**Training Q&A — the late history multiplier on Home Purchase Financing loans**

**What does the multiplier turn on?** On the number of late charges counted for the late history of the loan at the assessment date.

**What multiplier follows from the history?** Where two or more late charges are counted, the late history multiplier is 1.25; where exactly one is counted, the late history multiplier is 1.1. With none counted, no history multiplier applies.

**Where does the multiplier act?** On the late charge figure before its single rounding: the monthly principal-and-interest amount times the late charge rate divided by 100 is multiplied by it, the result is rounded half up to the cent once, and only then are the program's floor and cap applied.

| Late charges counted | Late history multiplier |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 1.25 |
| exactly 1 | 1.1 |
| none | none applies |

**Worked example (hypothetical).** A principal and interest of 420.31 at 5.00 percent is 21.0155; with one late charge counted it becomes 23.11705, rounded to 23.12; with two it becomes 26.269375, rounded to 26.27 — each then tested against the program's floor and cap.
